old: for God Almighty gives men their daily thoughts day by day
new: for God Almighty gives men their thoughts from day to day
reason: "daily" and "day by day" both state the same recurrence right next to each other, which reads as an accidental repetition rather than a deliberate rhetorical echo — it snags the ear on a first listen.

old: earrings fashioned into three brilliant pendants that sparkled beautifully
new: earrings, each fashioned into three brilliant pendants that sparkled beautifully
reason: As written it's ambiguous whether "three brilliant pendants" describes each earring or the whole gift (i.e., three earrings) — a listener has to stop and guess which noun "three" is counting.

old: Odysseus sought protection at Amphinomus of Dulichium’s knees
new: Odysseus sought protection at the knees of Amphinomus of Dulichium
reason: The possessive 's stacked onto the end of a name-plus-epithet phrase ("Amphinomus of Dulichium's knees") is hard to parse by ear — a listener briefly hears "Dulichium's knees" before the sense resolves.

old: son of Nisus, who was son of Aretias
new: son of Nisus son of Aretias
reason: The relative clause "who was son of Aretias" is meant to describe Nisus (giving Amphinomus's grandfather), but "who" sits close enough to "Amphinomus" that a first-time listener could momentarily attach it to the wrong person in the chain.
